build_interpretation: Mac final six-step build (5.914s) recompiles new core and both fixtures, archives and links both executables. It follows an initial 14-step build that stopped on a fixture compiler error, then a successful five-step completion with failing test counters. Final tests are accepted only after the final successful build.

Linux and Windows build/test drivers verify the same complete 117-file manifest before compiling and gate CTest on build success. Their logs record regenerated projects, affected existing inputs, new units and links.

Recent comparable six-step Mac builds took 3.729s (inventory) and 5.914s (this milestone). Exact workloads differ. Windows broad header-dependent build is 33.973s, Linux 14.372s. Source hashes, actual compiled units and executable records establish freshness, rather than elapsed time alone.

Focused builds compile all 28 core units, platform adapter, simulator, acquisition and refresh domain/native fixtures, and test host (35 units) without object caches. This is a new fixture-set baseline: Mac 151.455 s / Linux 159.675 s / Windows 68.533 s. Prior layout set with 35 different units took 65.882/151.535/69.694 s.

Longer Mac sanitizer wall time was investigated while its original compiler remained live and advanced to the acquisition fixture. Observed load was about 80 on 10 CPUs. Host contention may contribute, but causation is not proven; no restart or stale test was substituted.

mac_load_observation.interpretation: High host load may contribute to longer wall time. This is an observation, not proof of causal attribution. Build continues; no restart.

rejected_attempts.reason: Fixture optional aggregate initializer did not compile; corrected by explicit UnavailableObservation. Strict warnings unchanged; no CTest from the failed build accepted.

Fixture open counters included discovery opens. Assertions now capture the pre-acquisition baseline and require exactly three acquisition opens across cancellation/resume and exactly one for a completed 300-row preparation. These remain exact-count assertions.

guarantees: Sealed retained discovery directory is used for initial metadata-only binding of exactly requested native names; no original path reopen, display decoding or normalization substitution.
All request/row validation and count/name/display budget checks precede native acquisition. Duplicate requests fail, missing discovery names report uncertainty without probing.
Held metadata and recomputed hidden observation describe the object acquired now. Cached IDs do not certify continuity, and initial binding never preserves previously unheld row IDs/marks/focus.

Successful held families can subsequently refresh through PaneRefreshJob. Hard-link names remain separate. Native and inspection failures remain explicit named issues; unresolved discovery rows are retained.

Each advance has 256 steps plus an injected cooperative time slice; cancellation can resume incomplete requests, completed requests survive yields, exceptions poison before rethrow, and abandonment releases private owners.
Receiver generation gate rejects superseded/cancelled results; issued immutable results retain their owners independently.
limitations: This is worker-side initial binding preparation, not a scheduler, UI interaction or frozen operation source plan. Completed results may contain unresolved binding issues and unbound rows; no operation permission is inferred.
Mixed refresh of existing held families plus acquisition of new rows in one publication remains orchestration work.
Cached discovery IDs may have recycled before acquisition. Holding a newly opened object does not prove that it is the object seen in an earlier unheld observation.
Native calls/allocation/encoding can outlast the cooperative slice. Separate bounded name/index/row/issue copies are not a total memory quota or promise of OS handle capacity.

WP-01 remains open: self/descendant checks, native equivalence, operation-specific capabilities, remaining inventories, mixed acquisition/refresh, large-view indexes and UI/worker integration. WP-02 not started.
